subject: Outbound controls for Atlas Health private deployment - proxy/mTLS/DNS-TLS questions
messages:
From: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@atlashealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Outbound controls: Atlas Health private deployment questions

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment options last week. Our security and network teams are finalizing the allowlist and egress controls for the VPC/private connector. A few items we need clarified before we proceed with the POC: 

- Can Redwood support mutual TLS (client cert) from our outbound gateway to your control plane endpoints, rather than IP-only allowlisting? If yes, what cert format and rotation cadence do you expect?
- We expect to run behind an outbound transparent proxy (Envoy) that does DNS over TLS (DoT). Are your endpoints compatible with DoT and SNI passthrough?
- For compliance we need a minimal set of static egress IPs we can enter into our firewall (we cannot open wide ephemeral ranges). Can you provide a dedicated list for control-plane telemetry and another for model-serving callbacks?
- Any constraints on ephemeral port ranges, outbound UDP requirements, or blocked protocols we should be aware of?

Attaching our preliminary network template for your convenience (network-allowlist-template.csv). Can we get a short tech response and an ETA for a signed allowlist for the POC by EOD Thursday?

Thanks,
Sam Wilson
IT Architect, Atlas Health
Sam.Wilson@atlashealth.com
Attachment: network-allowlist-template.csv (CSV stub, 2KB)
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Wilson <sam.wilson@atlashealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 13:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Outbound controls: Atlas Health private deployment questions

Hi Sam —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; priyom and Marcus are looped for the detailed network artifacts. We can get you the signed allowlist for the POC by EOD Thu (Feb 5). Summary: 

- mTLS support: Yes. We support mutual TLS between customer egress gateway and our control plane (management/telemetry) endpoints. Required: client cert in PKCS#12 or PEM (RFC 7468) with chain; SNI must match the endpoint FQDN. See attached mtls-cert-guidelines.txt for exact CN/SAN requirements and rotation guidance.

- DoT & SNI: Our endpoints terminate TLS on the public IPs; DoT is fine as long as DNS resolution yields the canonical FQDNs we publish. We do not perform TLS interception; SNI preservation is required for traffic classification.

- Static egress IPs: We'll provide two sets: control-plane (management/metrics/logs) and data-plane (model-serving fallback/endpoints). For the POC we can reserve 3 static IPs for control-plane and 5 for data-plane. Marcus will enumerate them in the csv (egress-endpoints.csv).

- Ports/Protocols: Only outbound TCP 443 is required for TLS channels to Redwood-hosted endpoints. No UDP or non-TLS protocols are required for normal operation. Ephemeral source ports are expected (1024-65535) — if your firewall restricts ranges we can advise a narrower ephemeral window but prefer full ephemeral range for NAT stability.

Action items we will deliver by Thu EOD: 
- egress-endpoints.csv (static IPs + FQDNs) — Marcus
- mtls-cert-guidelines.txt — attached
- short one-page POC allowlist (signed-ready format) — Neha

If you prefer mTLS plus IP allowlist we can do both; mTLS is functionally sufficient for authentication but many customers want both for auditability.

Would you like a 30 min sync tomorrow morning to walk the security team through the cert fields?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachments: mtls-cert-guidelines.txt (text stub, 1KB)
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Feb 2026 08:05:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Atlas Health egress - technical notes (do not forward)

Neha / Marcus — internal notes to include in the CSV and the allowlist doc we hand to Atlas Health: 

- Endpoints: Split control-plane and data-plane FQDNs. Control-plane: api-control.redwood-inference.com (TLS only, client cert optional but supported). Data-plane (model-serving fallback): models-edge.redwood-inference.com.

- mTLS specifics: Accept PEM private key + cert chain; client cert must include O=Atlas Health and CN should be atlas-egress.<timestamp> or atlas-egress-<env>.Wildcard SANs not permitted. Rotation: recommended 90 days; we will accept up to 180 days but require push-update to our onboarding portal. We'll validate using mutual TLS handshake and map cert to account ID.

- Source IPs: For private deployments we can provide a dedicated /29 for control-plane (3 usable IPs) and a /28 for data-plane (13 usable IPs). Recommend offering 3 and 5 for the POC; for production, discuss reserved Dedicated egress pool.

- Ports: Only TCP/443 egress required. Additionally, if Atlas wants to use a TLS-terminated sidecar for observability (zipkin/prometheus push), allow outbound TCP 9411 and 9091 as optional. We should flag that in the CSV as optional columns.

- DNS over TLS: Fine. Important: the DNS server used by their egress must resolve our canonical FQDNs; if DoT returns internal/private addresses we need to validate. Do not perform TLS interception on traffic to our endpoints.

- Healthchecks: The POC will perform periodic heartbeats to control-plane on /health every 60s. These originate from one of the static IPs; include that path in the firewall allowlist.

Marcus — pls generate egress-endpoints.csv with columns: role, fqdn, ip, ports(required/optional), notes.

Thanks,
Priyom
Applied ML / Infra
